diagrams.title: **Do, read, ask
diagrams.caption: **Do, read, ask.** Tools perform actions, resources provide context without side effects, and prompt templates package good instructions for reuse.

diagrams.title: **Fill in the blanks, get consistent instructions
diagrams.caption: **Fill in the blanks, get consistent instructions.** The server owns the wording of the prompt; the client only supplies the values.

diagrams.title: **The server borrows the client's brain, with permission
diagrams.caption: **The server borrows the client's brain, with permission.** The user approves the AI task and reviews the output before anything goes back.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 360" aria-label="Sampling in a travel example. A travel server has a long list of Rome activities but no AI to rank them. It sends a sampling request to the MCP client: pick the 5 best activities for someone who likes history, art and food. The client asks the user to approve the AI task, runs the model, and shows the user the top five: Colosseum and Roman Forum, Vatican Museums, a Trastevere food tour, Borghese Gallery, and Campo de' Fiori market. diagrams.title: **A fence the client draws
diagrams.caption: **A fence the client draws.** The client tells the server which folder is the current workspace; inside it the server can work, outside it there's nothing for the server to touch.

diagrams.title: **Ask, don't assume
diagrams.caption: **Ask, don't assume.** Form mode collects fields through the client; URL mode keeps sensitive data away from the client entirely. Either way the client stays in control.
